title: Proper signed-word colimits attach alternating words along their boundaries
statement:
Let $\mathcal I$ be the category [def-nagata-category] of finite words in $+,-$, including the empty word $\epsilon$, with morphisms the weakly order-preserving maps of letter positions preserving signs. Composition is composition of maps of positions. For $n\geq0$ let $\mathcal I_{\leq n}$ be its full subcategory of words of length at most $n$. Let $E:\mathcal I\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be a functor to simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Assume $E$ is proper: every injective morphism $u$ induces a degreewise injective $E(u)$, and, for any two injections into the same word, the intersection of their image simplicial subsets is exactly the image of the injection of their common positions. Put $C_n(E)=\varinjlim_{\mathcal I_{\leq n}}E$, with colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $n\geq1$ let $a_n^+$ and $a_n^-$ be the length-$n$ alternating words starting with $+$ and $-$, respectively. For $e\in\{+,-\}$ let $B_n^e(E)\subseteq E(a_n^e)$ be the union of the images of $E(u)$ for all injections $u:w\hookrightarrow a_n^e$ with $|w|<n$, including $w=\epsilon$. The prescriptions sending $E(u)(x)$ to the image of $x\in E(w)$ in $C_{n-1}(E)$ define well-defined simplicial maps $B_n^e(E)\to C_{n-1}(E)$. For each $n\geq1$ the canonical square
$$\begin{matrix}
B_n^+(E)\amalg B_n^-(E)&\longrightarrow&C_{n-1}(E)\\
\big\downarrow&&\big\downarrow\\
E(a_n^+)\amalg E(a_n^-)&\longrightarrow&C_n(E)
\end{matrix}$$
is a pushout, meaning that maps from its lower-right corner to any simplicial set are uniquely determined by maps from its upper-right and lower-left corners agreeing on its upper-left corner. The left map is the coproduct of the two boundary inclusions; the right and bottom maps are induced by the colimit cocones. The construction is natural for natural transformations between proper functors. At degree zero, $C_0(E)=E(\epsilon)$.
